1.explanation: These are the two files that define and export the React DatePicker component in v11. In DatePicker.js the component is declared as a function but never wrapped in `React.forwardRef`, so refs passed to it never reach the inner input or calendar elements. In index.js it simply re-exports DatePicker; updating it (or the default export in DatePicker.js) to wrap the component in `forwardRef` is how refs can be forwarded to the underlying input element, restoring the v10 behavior.
1.bug_scenario: When upgrading from v10 to v11 of `@carbon/react`, attempting to pass a ref to the `<DatePicker>` yields the React warning: “Function components cannot be given refs. Attempts to access this ref will fail. Did you mean to use React.forwardRef()?” In v10 the DatePicker was forwarding its inner input node’s ref, but in v11 the DatePicker component is defined as a plain function and never wrapped in `forwardRef`, so the ref never reaches the underlying DOM input. The screenshot shows React complaining at render time that the ref isn’t being forwarded.

2.explanation: The file DatePicker.js defines the DatePicker component as a normal function but never wraps it in React.forwardRef, so it cannot receive or forward refs. The index.js in the same folder simply re-exports the component, so it also does not add ref support. To fix this bug, DatePicker.js must be wrapped with forwardRef and the passed ref forwarded down to the actual input element (or wrapper div) so that consumers can use ref the same way they did in v10.
2.bug_scenario: When upgrading from v10 to v11 of @carbon/react, passing a ref into <DatePicker> no longer works. The user sees the console warning: “Function components cannot be given refs… Did you mean to use React.forwardRef()?” In v10 DatePicker accepted refs (pointed at the inner input), but the v11 implementation is a plain functional component without forwardRef, so any ref passed to DatePicker is dropped and triggers the warning.
